```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(leaflet)
library(dplyr)

# Travel data with region info
travel_points <- data.frame(
  place = c(
    "Rome, Italy", "Cinque Terre, Italy", "Pisa, Italy", "Venice, Italy", "Murano, Italy",
    "Lima, Peru", "Ica, Peru", "Paracas, Peru", "Cuzco, Peru", "Sacred Valley, Peru", "Machu Picchu, Peru", "Aguas Calientes, Peru",
    "Honolulu, Hawaii", "Waikiki, Hawaii", "North Shore, Hawaii",
    "Sitka, Alaska", "Port Alexander, Alaska",
    "Whistler, Canada", "Vancouver, Canada"
  ),
  lat = c(
    41.9028, 44.1194, 43.7228, 45.4408, 45.4561,
    -12.0464, -14.0678, -13.8354, -13.5320, -13.2861, -13.1631, -13.1586,
    21.3069, 21.2767, 21.5940,
    57.0516, 56.2522,
    50.1163, 49.2827
  ),
  lon = c(
    12.4964, 9.7159, 10.4017, 12.3155, 12.3533,
    -77.0428, -75.7257, -76.2550, -71.9675, -72.0716, -72.5450, -72.5122,
    -157.8583, -157.8275, -158.1100,
    -135.3300, -134.6450,
    -122.9574, -123.1207
  ),
  region = c(
    rep("Europe", 5),
    rep("South America", 7),
    rep("Hawaii", 3),
    rep("Alaska", 2),
    rep("Canada", 2)
  )
)

region_colors <- c(
  "Europe" = "blue",
  "South America" = "green",
  "Hawaii" = "orange",
  "Alaska" = "purple",
  "Canada" = "red"
)

# Create the map with satellite imagery (no separate label overlay)
leaflet(travel_points) %>%
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    ~lon, ~lat,
    fillColor = "red",
    color = "white",
    radius = 6,
    weight = 1,
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.9,
    popup = ~paste0("<strong>", place, "</strong>"),
    clusterOptions = markerClusterOptions()
  )

```
